name: IBPS Clerk
fullName: Institute of Banking Personnel Selection – Common Recruitment Process for Customer Service Associates (CRP CSA / Clerk)
eligibility: Graduate in any discipline; 20–28 years (relaxation for reserved categories); proficiency in the official language of the state applied for

notification.summary: CRP CSA-XVI (Clerk 2026) notification came out in late July 2026 with online registration from 1 to 21 Aug 2026. The preliminary exam is scheduled for 10–11 Oct 2026 (in progress on the check date) and the mains is reported for 27 Dec 2026 (tentative). Dates are from news/education portals because ibps.in could not be reached from the research environment.

pattern.notes: 20 minutes per section with a separate timer. Sectional and overall cut-offs (state-wise) apply; prelims is qualifying only. No interview — final selection is on mains marks. Scores are normalised across shifts.

trendAnalysis.summary: The clerk prelims is easy-to-moderate; good attempts are usually 70–80. Numerical Ability is speed-driven: simplification/approximation (10–15 Qs), number series (5) and one or two DI sets, with the rest as short arithmetic word problems. Reasoning has 3–4 small puzzles/seating arrangements (box, floor, day-based, linear) carrying 12–15 questions, plus syllogism, inequality, coding, blood relations and quick misc questions. English is based on one RC (≈8–10 Qs), cloze, error spotting, fillers and rearrangement; word-swap and connector formats appeared more often recently.

resources.notes: IBPS does not release full question papers or answer keys for the clerk exam. Official material is limited to the Information Handout with sample questions and the pre-exam online practice test on ibps.in; candidates see their own scorecard. Previous papers in circulation are memory-based compilations by coaching portals.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question.

Cities are getting hotter faster than the countryside around them. Concrete, asphalt and glass absorb sunlight during the day and release it slowly at night, so urban neighbourhoods often stay several degrees warmer than nearby villages after sunset. This 'heat island' effect is not merely uncomfortable; it raises electricity demand for cooling, worsens air quality and can be deadly for outdoor workers and the elderly. Fortunately, some remedies are cheap. Painting roofs white reflects a large share of sunlight, and planting trees along streets provides both shade and cooling through evaporation. Several Indian cities have begun drafting heat action plans that combine such measures with early warnings and changes in working hours during heatwaves. Experts, however, caution that these plans succeed only when they are funded and enforced, not when they remain documents on a shelf.

According to the passage, why do urban neighbourhoods stay warmer than villages after sunset?
options: Cities receive more sunlight than villages
Concrete, asphalt and glass release the heat they absorbed during the day slowly
Trees in cities trap heat at night
questions.explanation: The passage says these materials 'absorb sunlight during the day and release it slowly at night'.

questions.question:
Read the passage and choose the word that best fits the numbered blank.

Saving money is easier when it becomes a (1) ______ rather than an occasional effort. Experts suggest setting aside a fixed amount as soon as the salary is (2) ______, instead of saving whatever is left at the end of the month. Automatic transfers to a recurring deposit can (3) ______ the temptation to spend.

Which word best fits blank (1)?
questions.explanation: 'A habit rather than an occasional effort' — habit is the natural contrast to occasional.

questions.question:
Read the passage and choose the word that best fits the numbered blank.

Saving money is easier when it becomes a (1) ______ rather than an occasional effort. Experts suggest setting aside a fixed amount as soon as the salary is (2) ______, instead of saving whatever is left at the end of the month. Automatic transfers to a recurring deposit can (3) ______ the temptation to spend.

Which word best fits blank (2)?
questions.explanation: One saves 'as soon as the salary is credited' (received in the account).

questions.question:
Read the passage and choose the word that best fits the numbered blank.

Saving money is easier when it becomes a (1) ______ rather than an occasional effort. Experts suggest setting aside a fixed amount as soon as the salary is (2) ______, instead of saving whatever is left at the end of the month. Automatic transfers to a recurring deposit can (3) ______ the temptation to spend.

Which word best fits blank (3)?
questions.explanation: Automatic transfers move money away before it can be spent, so they reduce the temptation to spend.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.
He has been working (A)/ in this bank since (B)/ the last five years (C)/ and plans to retire soon. (D)/ No error (E)
questions.explanation: A period of time ('the last five years') takes 'for', not 'since'. The error is in part B ('since' should be 'for').

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.
Each of the candidates (A)/ were asked to bring (B)/ two photographs and (C)/ a valid identity proof. (D)/ No error (E)
questions.explanation: 'Each of the…' is singular and takes 'was', so 'were asked' in part B is wrong.

questions.question:
Choose the option that best fills the blank.
The bank ______ its customers by SMS whenever a transaction is made.
questions.explanation: A singular subject ('The bank') with a habitual action takes the simple present 'alerts'.

questions.question:
Choose the pair that best fills both blanks.
The ______ rains damaged the standing crops, leaving farmers in ______.
questions.explanation: Rain that damages crops is 'unseasonal', and it leaves farmers 'in distress'. Other pairs are illogical.

questions.question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a meaningful paragraph and choose the FOURTH sentence.
A. She saved a small amount from her earnings every week.
B. Meena started a tailoring unit with a single sewing machine.
C. Today, her unit employs twelve women from her village.
D. Within two years, she had enough to buy three more machines.
E. She also took a small loan from a self-help group.
questions.explanation: Order: B (start) – A (savings) – E ('also' a loan) – D (bought machines) – C (today). Fourth sentence is D.

questions.question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a meaningful paragraph.
A. Therefore, it is wise to compare offers before signing up.
B. Credit cards can be useful if used responsibly.
C. However, they often carry very high interest on unpaid balances.
D. Fees and reward programmes also differ widely between banks.
E. They let users make purchases now and pay later.
questions.explanation: B introduces credit cards, E gives the benefit, C ('However') the drawback, D ('also') adds another difference, A ('Therefore') concludes: BECDA.

questions.question:
Choose the option that should replace the phrase in capitals to make the sentence correct.
She is SENIOR THAN ME in the office.
questions.explanation: Adjectives of Latin origin such as senior, junior and superior take 'to', not 'than': 'senior to me'.

questions.question:
Which pair of words should be interchanged to make the sentence meaningful?
The (A) cake baked a delicious (B) chef for the (C) guests at the (D) party.
questions.explanation: Swapping A and B: 'The chef baked a delicious cake for the guests at the party.'

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling has double 'c' and double 'm': Accommodate.

questions.question:
Choose the connector that correctly joins the sentences: 'The roads were slippery. The bus driver drove carefully.'
______ the roads were slippery, the bus driver drove carefully.
questions.explanation: The first sentence is the reason for the second, so 'Since' fits. 'Although/Despite/Whereas' show contrast and 'Unless' a condition.

12 men can finish a job in 15 days working 8 hours a day. In how many days will 20 men finish it working 6 hours a day?

Six boxes P, Q, R, S, T and U are placed one above another (position 1 is the bottom, 6 the top). R is placed fourth from the bottom. Only two boxes are placed between R and S. T is placed immediately above Q. U is not placed adjacent to S. P is placed somewhere below Q.

Which box is placed immediately below R?
questions.explanation: Bottom to top: S, P, U, R, Q, T. R is 4th, so S is 1st; Q–T must be 5th–6th (Q at 2nd would leave no place below it for P); U cannot be 2nd (adjacent to S), so U is 3rd and P 2nd. U is below R.

questions.question:
Six boxes P, Q, R, S, T and U are placed one above another (position 1 is the bottom, 6 the top). R is placed fourth from the bottom. Only two boxes are placed between R and S. T is placed immediately above Q. U is not placed adjacent to S. P is placed somewhere below Q.

How many boxes are placed between P and T?
questions.explanation: Bottom to top: S, P, U, R, Q, T. Between P (2nd) and T (6th) are U, R and Q — three boxes.

questions.question:
Six boxes P, Q, R, S, T and U are placed one above another (position 1 is the bottom, 6 the top). R is placed fourth from the bottom. Only two boxes are placed between R and S. T is placed immediately above Q. U is not placed adjacent to S. P is placed somewhere below Q.

Which box is placed at the top?
questions.explanation: Bottom to top: S, P, U, R, Q, T. T is at the top.

questions.question:
Six friends A, B, C, D, E and F attend a workshop on six consecutive days from Monday to Saturday, one person per day. B attends on Thursday. Only two persons attend between B and D. A attends on the day immediately after D. F attends on some day before E. C attends on some day after E.

Who attends the workshop on Wednesday?
questions.explanation: B is on Thursday, so D (three days away) is on Monday and A on Tuesday. F, E, C take Wednesday, Friday, Saturday in that order (F before E before C). F is on Wednesday.

questions.question:
Six friends A, B, C, D, E and F attend a workshop on six consecutive days from Monday to Saturday, one person per day. B attends on Thursday. Only two persons attend between B and D. A attends on the day immediately after D. F attends on some day before E. C attends on some day after E.

How many persons attend between A and E?
questions.explanation: Order: D (Mon), A (Tue), F (Wed), B (Thu), E (Fri), C (Sat). Between A and E are F and B — two persons.

questions.question:
Six friends A, B, C, D, E and F attend a workshop on six consecutive days from Monday to Saturday, one person per day. B attends on Thursday. Only two persons attend between B and D. A attends on the day immediately after D. F attends on some day before E. C attends on some day after E.

Who attends immediately before C?
questions.explanation: Order: D, A, F, B, E, C. E attends on Friday, just before C on Saturday.

questions.question: Among P, Q, R, S and T, each has a different height. Q is taller than only T. R is taller than Q but shorter than S. P is not the tallest. Who is the tallest?
questions.explanation: T is the shortest and Q second shortest. Among P, R, S: S > R and P is not the tallest, so S is the tallest.

questions.question:
Statements: All cats are dogs. All dogs are rats.
Conclusions: I. All cats are rats. II. Some rats are cats.
questions.explanation: Cats ⊂ dogs ⊂ rats, so all cats are rats (I) and therefore some rats are cats (II). Both follow.

questions.question:
Statements: Some pens are pencils. No pencil is an eraser.
Conclusions: I. Some pens are not erasers. II. Some erasers are pens.
questions.explanation: The pens that are pencils cannot be erasers, so I follows. There is no definite link between erasers and pens, so II does not follow.

questions.question:
Statement: M ≥ N > O = P ≤ Q
Conclusions: I. M > P  II. Q ≥ O
questions.explanation: M ≥ N > O = P gives M > P. Q ≥ P = O gives Q ≥ O. Both follow.

questions.question:
Statement: R < S ≤ T = U > V ≥ W
Conclusions: I. S < U  II. T > W
questions.explanation: S ≤ T = U gives S ≤ U, so 'S < U' is not definite (I fails). T = U > V ≥ W gives T > W (II follows).

questions.question: If 'PRINT' is coded as 'QSJOU', how is 'BLADE' coded?
questions.explanation: Each letter is moved one place forward: B→C, L→M, A→B, D→E, E→F = CMBEF.

questions.question: In a certain code, 'GARDEN' is written as 'FBQEDO'. How is 'MARKET' written in that code?
questions.explanation: Letters alternately move −1, +1: G−1=F, A+1=B, R−1=Q, D+1=E, E−1=D, N+1=O. MARKET → L, B, Q, L, D, U = LBQLDU.

questions.question: Pointing to a woman, Aman said, 'She is the only daughter of my paternal grandfather's only son.' How is the woman related to Aman?
questions.explanation: The only son of Aman's paternal grandfather is Aman's father; his only daughter is Aman's sister.

questions.question: P is the mother of Q. Q is the sister of R. R is the father of S. T is the wife of R. How is P related to S?
questions.explanation: P is the mother of Q and R. R is S's father, so P is S's grandmother.

questions.question: Sita is facing north. She turns 90° clockwise, then 180° anticlockwise and then 45° clockwise. Which direction is she facing now?
questions.explanation: North → 90° clockwise = East → 180° anticlockwise = West → 45° clockwise = North-West.

questions.question: Five friends scored different marks. A scored more than B but less than C. D scored less than B. E scored more than C. Who scored the second highest marks?
questions.explanation: Order: E > C > A > B > D. C is second highest.

questions.question:
Arrangement: B 7 # D 3 K @ 9 M 2 $ P 5 R & 8 T
Which element is 4th to the right of the 10th element from the left?
questions.explanation: The 10th element from the left is 2; the 4th to its right is the 14th element, R.

questions.question: If the English alphabet is written in reverse order (Z to A), which letter will be 8th to the right of the 15th letter from the left?
questions.explanation: In reverse order, position k holds the letter numbered 27 − k. 15 + 8 = 23rd position → letter number 4 = D.

questions.question: In the number 5726436, 1 is added to each odd digit and 1 is subtracted from each even digit. How many digits appear more than once in the new number?
questions.explanation: 5→6, 7→8, 2→1, 6→5, 4→3, 3→4, 6→5 gives 6815345. Only 5 appears twice, so one digit repeats.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: 27, 125, 196, 343, 1331
questions.explanation: 27, 125, 343 and 1331 are cubes of odd numbers (3³, 5³, 7³, 11³); 196 (= 14²) is not a cube.
